The Shevaroy hills are located in Tamil Nadu and form part of the Eastern Ghats mountain range. Under her leadership, Darpana Academy has contributed significantly to the preservation and promotion of Indian classical dance forms and performing arts.

Tendu leaves (Diospyros melanoxylon) are used as wrappers for making bidis, which are traditional hand-rolled cigarettes popular in India. These leaves are particularly suitable for this purpose due to their durability, flexibility, and ability to retain their shape when rolled. questions.question: What are the five Fs of indirect transmission? अप्रत्यक्ष संचरण के पाँच F क्या हैं?
questions.solution: In epidemiology, the five Fs represent the primary routes of indirect disease transmission. This concept is fundamental in understanding disease transmission and implementing preventive measures.

questions.question: If m + n = 24, then (m - 16) 3 + (n - 8) 3 is _____. यदि m + n = 24, तो (m - 16) 3 + (n - 8) 3 _____ है।
questions.solution:
Let m + n = 24

=> (a + b)3 = a3 + b3 + 3ab(a + b)

Let a = m - 16 and b = n - 8

Given m + n = 24, we need to express m and n in terms of a and b.

=> m = a + 16

=> n = b + 8

=> (a + 16) + (b + 8) = 24

=> a + b + 24 = 24

=> a + b = 0

=> b = -a

Now, substitute b in the given expression:

(a - 16)3 + (n - 8)3 = a3 + (-a)3

=> a3 + (-a)3

=> a3 - a3

=> 0

Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

Five years later, I was eating this same dish at the same restaurant.
questions.solution:
The correct option to replace the highlighted segment is am eating.

The highlighted segment "was eating" is in the past continuous tense, which is used to describe an action that was ongoing at a specific point in the past. However, in this case, the phrase "Five years later" refers to the future from a previous reference point. Hence, the tense needs to reflect this correctly.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an adverbial usage error. "Mr. Arun / will pay dear / for his / financial mistake."
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into four segments. Identify the segment that contains an adverbial usage error.

"Mr. Arun / will pay dear / for his / financial mistake."
questions.solution: The error is in the segment "will pay dear." The correct adverbial form should be "dearly." When modifying a verb (pay), we should use the adverb form "dearly" rather than the adjective form "dear." The phrase "pay dearly" is an established expression meaning "to suffer serious consequences." All other segments are grammatically correct.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. My sisters wished me good luck before I went on the stage to sing.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.

My sisters wished me good luck before I went on the stage to sing.

options.text: Told me to sit on the fence
options.html: Told me to sit on the fence

options.text: Told me to break a leg
options.html: Told me to break a leg

options.text: Told me to break the ice
options.html: Told me to break the ice

options.text: Told me to break an arm
options.html: Told me to break an arm

questions.solution: "Break a leg" is the appropriate theatrical idiom used to wish someone good luck before a performance. It's considered a traditional way to wish performers well. The other options are different idioms with unrelated meanings: "sit on the fence" means to avoid taking sides, "break the ice" means to initiate social interaction, and "break an arm" is not a standard idiom.

questions.question: Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words. "The list of subjects to be discussed at a meeting"
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

"The list of subjects to be discussed at a meeting"
questions.solution:
Let's understand the meaning of each option:

Minutes - official record of the proceedings of a meeting

Objectives - aims or goals

Agenda - a list of items to be discussed at a meeting

Menu - a list of food items available

"Agenda" is the correct one-word substitute as it specifically refers to a planned series of items or schedule of matters to be discussed at a meeting. The other options have different meanings unrelated to the pre-meeting discussion list.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. "The drug pedlar was arrested by the narcotics team."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

"The drug pedlar was arrested by the narcotics team."

options.text: The narcotics team was arrested the drug pedlar.
options.html: The narcotics team was arrested the drug pedlar.

options.text: The narcotics team arrest the drug pedlar.
options.html: The narcotics team arrest the drug pedlar.

options.text: The narcotics team arrested the drug pedlar.
options.html: The narcotics team arrested the drug pedlar.

options.text: The narcotics team has arrested the drug pedlar.
options.html: The narcotics team has arrested the drug pedlar.

questions.solution: The given sentence is in passive voice (subject + was/were + past participle + by + agent). To convert it to active voice, we need to make the agent (narcotics team) the subject and use the correct past tense form. Since the passive sentence uses "was arrested" (simple past), the active voice should use "arrested" (simple past). Option 3 correctly makes this conversion while maintaining the same temporal meaning.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. She has _______ (witty) remarks about everything.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.

She has _______ (witty) remarks about everything.
questions.solution: The word "witty" means cleverly amusing or humorous. Its antonym should express the opposite meaning. "Unamusing" directly contradicts "witty" as it means not funny or entertaining. The other options don't serve as proper antonyms: "sorry" expresses regret, "whimsical" means playfully quaint, and "woeful" means full of sorrow - none of these are direct opposites of "witty."

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. "We have postponed this movie outing too many times, so we are going tomorrow, come _____ or shine."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

"We have postponed this movie outing too many times, so we are going tomorrow, come _____ or shine."
questions.solution: "Come rain or shine" is an idiomatic expression meaning "regardless of the weather" or "no matter what happens." It's a fixed expression that always uses "rain" and "shine" as the contrasting elements. The other options don't form part of this established idiom and would not make sense in this context.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks. "He had ________ the ________ into smaller clips."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blanks.

"He had ________ the ________ into smaller clips."
questions.solution: The sentence requires a past participle in the first blank (following "had") and a noun in the second blank (as the object being divided). "Clipped" is the past participle form needed after "had" in a past perfect construction, and "clipping" as a noun refers to the item being divided into smaller pieces.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence. (P) the sun (Q) to our planet, Earth (O) provides essential energy (R) sustaining life and warmth
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Select the option that arranges the parts in the correct sequence.

(P) the sun

(Q) to our planet, Earth

(O) provides essential energy

(R) sustaining life and warmth
questions.solution: The correct sequence "The sun provides essential energy to our planet, Earth, sustaining life and warmth" forms a logical and grammatically complete sentence. This arrangement follows proper subject-verb-object structure, with "the sun" as the subject, "provides" as the verb, and the remaining parts completing the meaning.

questions.question: Question 87

options.text: a, c, g, b, h, i, f, e, d, j
options.html: a, c, g, b, h, i, f, e, d, j

options.text: a, b, d, c, e, f, h, g, i, j
options.html: a, b, d, c, e, f, h, g, i, j

options.text: a, b, d, c, g, e, f, h, i, j
options.html: a, b, d, c, g, e, f, h, i, j

options.text: a, g, b, c, i, d, e, f, h,j
options.html: a, g, b, c, i, d, e, f, h,j

questions.solution:
A meaningful sentence should follow a logical order, keeping subject-verb agreement and proper sentence flow in mind.

A correct sentence could be:

"I heard that the chef is going to work in the new restaurant across the road."

"I heard" (a, g) → This forms the subject and verb of the sentence, establishing who is doing the action.

"that" (b) → This conjunction connects the main clause with the dependent clause.

"the chef" (c) → This is the subject of the dependent clause, indicating who is involved.

"is going" (i) → This verb phrase describes what the chef is doing.

"to work" (d) → Explains the purpose of the chefs action.

"in the new restaurant" (e, f, h) → Specifies the location where the chef is going to work.

"across the road" (j) → Adds more detail about the location.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. O. went P. yesterday Q. we R. to the S. park
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

O. went

P. yesterday

Q. we

R. to the

S. park
questions.solution: The correct sequence is QORSP - "We went to the park yesterday." The sequence forms a grammatically correct sentence following Subject (we) + Verb (went) + Object/Place (to the park) + Time (yesterday). The subject "we" comes first, followed by the action "went." Then comes the prepositional phrase "to the park" indicating place, and finally the time adverb "yesterday." The other options create ungrammatical sequences that don't make logical sense.

questions.question: Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence. A. needs to be B. the shelf in C. a piece of wood D. the kitchen E. need to buy F. replaced, so I will
questions.questionHtml:
Parts of a sentence are given below in jumbled order. Arrange the parts in the correct order to form a meaningful sentence.

A. needs to be

B. the shelf in

C. a piece of wood

D. the kitchen

E. need to buy

F. replaced, so I will
questions.solution: The correct sequence "BDAFEC" forms the sentence: "The shelf in the kitchen needs to be replaced, so I will need to buy a piece of wood." The sentence follows logical progression: identifying the object (shelf) and its location (kitchen), stating what needs to be done (needs to be replaced), and then describing the consequent action (buying wood).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Paralysed
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word.

Paralysed
questions.solution:
Paralysed - unable to move or function normally

Demure - reserved, modest, or shy

Stifled - suppressed or restrained

Sultry - hot and humid

Healthy - in good health, functioning normally

The word "healthy" is the most appropriate antonym for "paralysed" as it indicates normal functioning and well-being, which is opposite to the inability to move or function. The other options have different meanings unrelated to the concept of paralysis.

questions.question: Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence. "One must be confident of winning and gaining one's goals and must face situations, disasters, trials and setbecks of life with confidence."
questions.questionHtml:
Select the INCORRECTLY spelt word in the given sentence.

"One must be confident of winning and gaining one's goals and must face situations, disasters, trials and setbecks of life with confidence."
questions.solution: The word "setbecks" is incorrectly spelled. The correct spelling is "setbacks." A setback means a reversal or check in progress. The word comes from "set" + "back" meaning something that moves progress backward or causes a delay. All other words - trials, disasters, and confident - are spelled correctly. A trial means a test or examination, disaster means a sudden accident or natural catastrophe, and confident means feeling or showing confidence.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word. Repulse
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the given word.

Repulse
questions.solution: "Repulse" means to drive back or reject with force. "Repel" most accurately matches this meaning as it also means to drive back or ward off. The other options have different meanings: "Substitute" means to replace something, "Recover" means to regain or get back, and "Reprove" means to scold or criticize.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank. Listening to the same lecture everyday appeared very ___________ to him. (boring)
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the word in brackets to fill in the blank.

Listening to the same lecture everyday appeared very ___________ to him. (boring)
questions.solution: The word "boring" suggests something tedious or uninteresting due to lack of variety. "Monotonous" most appropriately captures this meaning as it refers to something tediously uniform or lacking in variety. The other options convey entirely different meanings: "furious" means angry, "nervous" relates to anxiety, and "monolithic" means large and uniform.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word. Many people love to visit enchanting hills.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate synonym of the underlined word.

Many people love to visit enchanting hills.
questions.solution: The word "enchanting" means captivating or delightfully charming. Among the given options, "alluring" is the most appropriate synonym as it also means attractively fascinating or charming. The other options convey entirely different meanings: "cool" refers to temperature or being fashionable, "risky" means dangerous, and "echoing" relates to sound reflection.
